key_insight: Static atomic buses let neutral-atom systems perform long-range fault-tolerant operations without moving qubits, reducing the latency and heating that limit atom-shuttling designs.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable hardware route for high-fidelity stabilizer readout, logical gates, and modular fault-tolerant architectures in neutral-atom quantum computers.
method: Auxiliary mediator atoms implement long-range controlled-Z gates between static qubits.
Co-designed optimal-control pulses enforce time-optimality, interaction flatness, and robustness.
Architecture-level simulations assess LDPC stabilizers and neighboring surface-code patch operations under realistic noise.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports bus-gate fidelities approaching 99.9% in a few hundred nanoseconds and predicts over an order-of-magnitude logical error-rate improvement versus shuttling architectures, with QEC cycles around 1 ms for code distances d<12.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on precise control of mediator dynamics and may be sensitive to calibration, noise model assumptions, and hardware implementation complexity.
paper_title: Fault-tolerant quantum computation with static atomic buses
